cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is up on Mount Sinai inside the cloud, and he stays there forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24:18). That's where the LORD speaks to him. First order of business: tell the Israelites to bring Him an offering.

cards.question: God wants an offering from the Israelites. Who is Moses supposed to receive it from?

answers.text: Anyone whose heart moves him to give
Each man who is twenty or older
The leaders of the twelve tribes

cards.text: Then God lists what they can bring: gold, silver and bronze, colored yarn, fine linen, goat hair, leather, acacia wood, olive oil, spices and gemstones. When I left the junk drawer, the most valuable thing I owned was a stubby pencil, and I BORROWED that.

cards.question: God tells Moses the Israelites are to make Him a sanctuary so that He may ___ among them.
God tells Moses to design the tabernacle and its furnishings however he thinks best.

cards.text: First up: an ark of acacia wood, covered in pure gold inside AND out. INSIDE, friend, where nobody even looks, and I've had cookie crumbs in my apron pocket since the Millers' kitchen.
God tells Moses to cast four gold rings for the ark's feet, two on each side, and to make poles of acacia wood covered in gold.

cards.question: The gold-covered poles slide into the rings on the sides of the ark. What are they for?
Once the poles are in the ark's rings, they get pulled out whenever the ark is set down.
God also tells Moses to place something inside the ark. What goes in?

answers.text: The Testimony God will give Moses

cards.text: Next comes a mercy seat of pure gold, the same length and width as the ark. At each end of it goes a cherub of hammered gold.

cards.question: The two cherubim and the mercy seat are all made from ___ piece of gold.
The cherubim on the mercy seat face away from each other, looking out toward the people.

cards.text: Then the mercy seat goes right on top of the ark, with the Testimony inside. Lid on, everything sealed in place, and I'm getting emotional over here because sealing boxes is my WHOLE job.

cards.question: God points to a place above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim over the ark. What does He say will happen there?

cards.text: Next piece of furniture: a table of acacia wood, covered in pure gold, with a rim, a gold molding and four gold rings at its legs.

cards.question: Like the ark, the table gets gold-covered poles of acacia wood so it can be carried.

cards.text: God also wants plates, dishes, pitchers and bowls for the table, all of pure gold. PURE GOLD dishes, friend, and I hand out my cookies on a napkin I found in the junk drawer.

cards.question: What are the gold pitchers and bowls for the table used for?
God tells Moses to place something on the table before Him. What is it?
The Bread of the Presence stays on the table before God at ___ times.

cards.text: Then comes a lampstand of pure hammered gold, from its base and shaft right up to its cups, buds and petals.

cards.question: The lampstand is built from separate gold parts that get joined together.

cards.text: It gets six branches, three on each side, with cups shaped like almond blossoms on every branch and on the lampstand itself. This is fancier than anything I've ever stamped, and I once did a snowflake that took me THREE tries.

cards.question: God tells Moses to set seven lamps on the lampstand so they ___ the area in front of it.

cards.text: Even the wick trimmers and their trays are pure gold, and the lampstand and all its tools come from a talent of gold. A TALENT of gold, friend, and my only talent is dropping chocolate chips on the floor.

cards.question: To wrap it up, God gives Moses one more reminder about all of it. What is it?

answers.text: Finish the work in forty days
Let only the priests build it

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. God's not done talking, friend, and Moses is still up on that mountain.

findings.problem: Every joke in the walkthrough uses the same template: Papa Dorin names a costly gold item, then puts down some humble thing he owns or does (stop 1 card 3 pencil, stop 1 card 6 apron crumbs, stop 2 card 3 napkin, stop 2 card 9 snowflake, stop 2 card 11 talent). The punchline shape repeats five times, so the jokes read as a formula and not as reactions fitted to each moment.

rule.text: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question. There are no joke quotas and no required kinds of jokes.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new backstory fact: that the stubby pencil was the most valuable thing he owned when he left the junk drawer, and that he borrowed it. The backstory only says he used the pencil to write his note. It never says he took the pencil with him or owned anything when he left.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke says he has had cookie crumbs in his apron pocket since the Millers' kitchen. This adds a new backstory detail, and it conflicts with the backstory, which says he came out of the drawer renewed with 'his apron clean.' The line 'where nobody even looks' also states something about the ark's inside that the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The whole passage is tabernacle building plans, which prep-walkthrough.md lists as a long stretch: summed up in one story card, never a choice card, and never a stop of its own. The walkthrough instead gives the plan details many choice cards (poles, rings, one piece of gold, which way the cherubim face, carrying the table, the lampstand's construction). Applying the long-stretch rule strictly would leave the passage with almost no walkthrough, which conflicts with the stop guidance and the goal of understanding the passage.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a long-stretch type (here, building plans for the tabernacle), should the long-stretch rule apply at all? If not, which details may get choice cards: only the heart of God's speech (the willing offering, dwelling among them, meeting above the mercy seat, the Bread of the Presence, the pattern), or the construction details too?

findings.problem: This final card is only the 'story isn't over' line, which is allowed when the last verse is asked on a choice card. It cites Exodus 25:40 even though it tells nothing from that verse. Its mention of Moses on the mountain comes from Exodus 24:18 context.
findings.question: What should the verses field be on a final story card that holds only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no part of the passage?
